profile.summary: BioEmu-2 is a generative model from Microsoft Research that produces three dimensional all-atom structures for a biomolecular system given its chemical composition. Rather than returning a single predicted structure, it samples an ensemble of plausible structures by reverse diffusion, so a user can look at how a system moves between states; it can also propagate a set of sampled structures forward in time. The input is one or more biomolecular sequences, optionally with a multiple sequence alignment, contact conditioning and method conditioning, and systems may contain proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and other chemical components.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model card describes BioEmu-2 as a diffusion-based all-atom score model with approximately 500M parameters. Structures are generated by reverse diffusion from noise, conditioned on the chemical composition of the system and optionally on an alignment, on contacts between specific atoms and on a method label. Because sampling is generative, the same input can be sampled many times to give an ensemble rather than one answer, and the authors say structure prediction can be guided by user-supplied information about distances between specific atoms. The code also offers steering samplers that favour structures with chosen properties, and an implicit transfer operator mode that generates a structure a chosen lag time later.

sections.title: What it was trained on
sections.body: The model card lists the training sets with the number of training sequences or systems in each. Experimental structures come from the PDB in the Boltz-1 preprocessing (189,745 systems). Seven sets of molecular dynamics trajectories generated inside Microsoft contribute between 170 and 7,164 systems each. The largest contributions are AI-predicted structures: 7,231,107 AFDB monomers, 753,271 AFDB homodimer multiconformation systems, 22,157 AFDB heterodimer systems and 50,651 Teddymer systems. The card states that training used only publicly available data and data generated in-house by Microsoft, and that the training dates were August to September 2026.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is published, named bioemu2-preview, which load_model downloads by default from the microsoft/bioemu2 repository on Hugging Face. The model card gives no version number for the model itself, states a release date of October 2026 and says the same checkpoint was used for every benchmark it reports. A result should therefore name the code commit, the checkpoint name and the Hugging Face revision; this page read code at commit 8d4a2b7238716a94543ceaf411dfe32f99c1ae7c and the Hugging Face repository at revision dd4b0c1b69984b68edcb6200a544213be4d75242. Sampling is stochastic, so a reproducible run must also fix the sampler and the number of samples; the checkpoint documentation shows the precision defaults, which can be changed to full precision.

facts.value: All-atom score model trained for diffusion, sampled by reverse diffusion, with optional conditioning on an alignment, on contacts and on a method label. Pair representations can be split across GPUs by context parallelism.

limitations.text: Sampling frequencies are not calibrated probabilities: the model card says they must not be read as Boltzmann probabilities or quantitative free energies, and that binding affinity prediction is out of scope.
limitations.source_locator: MODEL_CARD.md: Known limitations and Out-of-scope use cases

quotes.text: **Uncalibrated ensembles:** sampling frequency must not be interpreted as a calibrated Boltzmann probability or quantitative free energy.
It does not generate sequences, and it does not predict binding affinities.

limitations.text: Quality depends on the alignment and on how well the system is represented in the training data: the card expects worse results for shallow or poor alignments, including orphan proteins, engineered constructs and some viral proteins, and says performance on under-represented sequence classes is uncertain.

quotes.text: **MSA dependence:** quality is expected to fall for shallow or poor MSAs, including orphan proteins, engineered constructs, and some viral proteins.
**Training-distribution bias:** PDB, AFDB, and Microsoft-generated MD data over-represent well-studied protein families.

limitations.text: It is a research release. The card states it is not intended or validated for clinical or patient decisions and that commercial or real-world use is not recommended without further testing, and outputs should be treated as computational hypotheses.

run_guide.summary: Install BioEmu2 on a Linux GPU machine and sample eight equilibrium conformations of adenylate kinase from its PDB entry.
prerequisites: Linux with an NVIDIA GPU; macOS and Windows are not supported.
Python 3.12, 3.13 or 3.14. The developers tested and evaluated benchmark metrics with Python 3.12.
A GPU of compute capability 7.5 or newer for the cuda extra, or 7.0 with the cuda12 extra; the smallest device the developers tested was an 80 GB A100.
Network access: the checkpoint is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use.
At least four GPUs if context-parallel sampling is needed for a system that does not fit on one device.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/bioemu2.git
cd bioemu2
git checkout --detach 8d4a2b7238716a94543ceaf411dfe32f99c1ae7c
steps.explanation: The README's install commands are run from the repository root, so the clone and the checkout of the commit this page read were added here.

quotes.text: Run the installation command for your GPU from the repository root.

steps.title: Create and activate a virtual environment
steps.explanation: The README recommends an isolated environment and gives these two commands for creating one from the repository root.

quotes.text:
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

steps.title: Install with the CUDA extra
steps.explanation: Installs BioEmu2 for GPUs of compute capability 7.5 or newer. On compute capability 7.0, such as a V100, the README gives the cuda12 extra with the PyTorch CUDA 12.6 index instead.

quotes.text: python -m pip install ".[cuda]"
on these GPUs, use the `cuda12` extra with the PyTorch CUDA 12.6 package index:

steps.title: Sample an equilibrium ensemble
steps.explanation: The README's quick start command. It downloads the bioemu2-preview checkpoint on first use and samples eight equilibrium conformations of adenylate kinase into the output directory.

quotes.text:
bioemu2 sample-equilibrium \
  --pdb-id 1AKE \
  --out outputs/adk

By default it
downloads the `bioemu2-preview` checkpoint

steps.title: Predict a single folded structure
steps.explanation: The README's second quick start command, for the structure prediction mode rather than ensemble sampling. Run bioemu2 --help to list all commands.

quotes.text:
bioemu2 predict-structure \
  --pdb-id 1UBQ \
  --num-samples 1 \
  --out outputs/ubiquitin
Run `bioemu2 --help` to list all commands.

outputs: samples.xtc and topology.cif in each output directory, written by the sampling commands.
A cached copy of the bioemu2-preview checkpoint in the Hugging Face cache; the log reports where it was stored.

Sampling is stochastic: repeated runs give different structures unless the sampler and seed are fixed.
The commands assume a supported Linux machine with an NVIDIA GPU; the README states macOS and Windows are not supported.
